title: Taco Dip
description: A creamy, cheesy taco dip with seasoned ground beef, Fiesta Ranch, and Rotel. Serve chilled with tortilla chips.

ingredients.name: Rotel diced tomatoes and green chilies

steps: Brown the ground beef in a skillet over medium heat, seasoning with salt and black pepper to taste. Drain excess grease.
In a large bowl, combine sour cream, Fiesta Ranch seasoning mix, Rotel, and shredded cheddar cheese.
Add the cooked ground beef and mix until everything is evenly combined.
Refrigerate until ready to serve. Serve chilled with tortilla chips.

title: Baked Bacon Mac & Cheese
description: Extra-creamy baked cheddar mac and cheese with a full pound of bacon, a silky sodium-citrate cheese sauce, and a golden cheesy topping.

ingredients.name: shredded cheddar cheese, divided (1 lb for sauce; ½ lb for topping)
heavy cream, as needed for sauce consistency

steps: Preheat the oven to 375°F. Cook the elbow pasta in salted water until about 2–3 minutes shy of fully cooked; drain.
In a saucepan, bring the chicken broth to a low simmer. Stir in the sodium citrate, then gradually add 1 lb of the shredded cheddar, stirring until melted and smooth.

Gradually add 1–2 cups of heavy cream to moderate the temperature and thin the sauce. Stir in 2 tablespoons of reserved bacon grease and all 3 tablespoons of butter. Aim for a sauce slightly thinner than nacho cheese; it will thicken in the oven.
Combine the pasta, cheese sauce, and chopped cooked bacon. Fold gently and season to taste with salt, black pepper, garlic powder, and paprika.
Transfer to a casserole dish and top with the remaining ½ lb of shredded cheddar.
Bake at 375°F for about 45 minutes, until heated through and bubbly.

title: Homemade Hollandaise Sauce
description: A rich, buttery, lemony hollandaise made gently in one saucepan with constant stirring.
steps: Add the butter chunks, water, lemon juice, and egg yolks to a saucepan.
Heat over very low heat, stirring constantly as the butter melts and the sauce comes together.
Remove the pan from the heat as needed to keep it from overheating or scrambling the eggs. Continue stirring until the sauce is smooth and slightly thickened.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste. Serve promptly.

title: Chicken Gnocchi Soup
description: Rich and creamy chicken gnocchi soup with tender vegetables, Parmesan, spinach, and pillowy potato gnocchi.

ingredients.name: chicken breasts, cooked and diced or shredded
black pepper, plus more to taste
potato gnocchi, cooked according to package directions

steps: In a large pot over medium heat, sauté the diced onion, matchstick carrots, and celery with a little salt and pepper for about 8 minutes, until beginning to soften. Add the minced garlic and cook for 1 minute more.
Add the cooked chicken, garlic powder, black pepper, and Italian seasoning. Pour in the chicken broth and simmer for 10 minutes.
Stir in the heavy whipping cream, shredded Parmesan, and cooked potato gnocchi. Keep at a gentle simmer for another 15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the soup starts to thicken.
Stir in the roughly chopped spinach and cook for another 10 minutes. Taste and adjust salt and other seasonings before serving.

title: Gringo Chicken Enchiladas
description: Creamy, cheesy chicken-filled flour tortillas baked with green enchilada sauce and Colby Jack. A cozy, Midwest-style take on enchiladas.

ingredients.name: cooking spray or oil, for greasing casserole dish

steps: Preheat the oven to 350°F and lightly grease a casserole dish.

In a large bowl, mix the cooked shredded chicken with half of the green enchilada sauce (14 oz), the cream of chicken soup, half a packet of taco seasoning, and half of the shredded Colby Jack cheese (4 oz).
Divide the filling among the flour tortillas. Roll each tortilla and arrange seam-side down in the prepared casserole dish.
Pour the remaining green enchilada sauce (14 oz) over the rolled tortillas and sprinkle with the remaining 4 oz of Colby Jack cheese.
Bake at 350°F for 20 minutes, until hot and the cheese is melted.

title: Homemade Pancakes
description: Fluffy, buttery homemade pancakes with a tender crumb. Keep the batter a little lumpy for the best texture.
steps: In a large bowl, whisk together the flour, sugar, salt, baking powder, and baking soda.
In a separate bowl, mix the milk, oil, vanilla, apple cider vinegar, and eggs.
Pour the wet ingredients into the dry ingredients and fold together gently. Do not overmix; the batter should remain a little lumpy.
Heat a skillet over medium heat and add butter. Pour in portions of batter and gently move each pancake around to soak up some of the melted butter.
Cook until bubbles form and the edges begin to set, then flip and cook the other side until golden and cooked through. Repeat with remaining batter, adding more butter as needed.

title: Grandpa's Waffles
description: Light, fluffy homemade waffles with whipped egg whites folded into the batter. The recipe calls for 2 tablespoons of sugar, but Grandpa may have snuck in a little more.
steps: Preheat your waffle iron according to the manufacturer's instructions.
In a large bowl, whisk together the flour, baking powder, sugar, and salt.
Separate the eggs. In a small mixing bowl, combine the egg yolks, milk, melted butter, and vanilla.
Using a mixer, beat the egg whites in a separate clean bowl until stiff peaks form.
Pour the milk mixture into the dry ingredients and stir just until combined.
Gently fold the beaten egg whites into the batter. Do not overmix or the whites will deflate; it's okay if some streaks of egg white remain visible.
Cook the batter in the preheated waffle iron according to its instructions, until the waffles are golden and cooked through.

title: Cast Iron Deep Dish Pizza
description: A hearty Chicago-style deep-dish pizza baked in a 12-inch cast iron skillet, with a buttery Parmesan-coated crust, plenty of mozzarella, your favorite toppings, and a full batch of homemade tomato sauce. Makes one pizza, cut into four generous slices.

ingredients.name: crushed tomatoes, preferably Cento San Marzano (sauce)

steps: CRUST — In a bowl, mix the flour, salt, and instant yeast. Add the oil and mix until crumbly, then add the warm water.
Knead the dough for 5 minutes. Place in a covered bowl and rest for 5 minutes. Knead for another 5 minutes, form into a ball, cover, and let rise for 2 hours.
SAUCE — Melt 2 tablespoons of butter in a small pot. Add the finely diced onion, salt, oregano, and crushed red pepper. Cook for about 5 minutes.

Add the minced garlic and cook for another minute. Stir in the entire 28-ounce can of crushed tomatoes and the sugar. Reduce heat to medium-low and simmer for 45 minutes, covering if the sauce splatters.
ASSEMBLY — Preheat the oven to 425°F. Roll the dough into a circle about 14 inches across.
Spread the softened half-stick of butter around the inside of a 12-inch cast iron skillet, then sprinkle Parmesan over the butter.
Press the dough into the skillet, bringing it up the sides, and trim off any excess dough.
Layer the shredded low-moisture mozzarella over the crust, followed by your pizza toppings. Spread all of the prepared sauce on top and finish with another sprinkle of Parmesan.
Bake for 35–40 minutes. Let the pizza cool in the skillet for 15 minutes before cutting into 4 generous slices.

title: Chicken Stuff
description: An easy slow-cooker chicken with salsa, black beans, and corn. Serve it over rice or a baked potato. Shred the chicken to your desired shredness—or until your back hurts.
steps: Add the chicken breasts, salsa, rinsed and drained black beans, drained corn (or frozen corn), and chicken broth to the slow cooker.
Cover and cook on LOW for 4–5 hours, until the chicken is cooked through and reaches 165°F in the thickest part.
Shred the chicken with two forks or whatever works best, until it reaches your desired shredness—or your back hurts.
Stir the shredded chicken back into the slow cooker. Keep on WARM until ready to serve.
Serve over cooked rice or a baked potato.

title: Homemade Lasagna
description: A classic layered lasagna with a rich beef-and-Italian-sausage tomato sauce, creamy ricotta filling, and shredded mozzarella. Baked in a 9×13-inch dish; serves 8–10.
steps: Preheat oven to 375°F.
In a large skillet or pot, slowly brown the ground beef and Italian sausage. Spoon off excess fat.
Add the minced garlic, dried basil, 1½ teaspoons salt, tomatoes, and tomato paste. Simmer uncovered for 30 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Meanwhile, cook the lasagna noodles in plenty of boiling salted water until tender. Drain and rinse.
Beat the eggs in a bowl. Mix in the ricotta, Parmesan or Romano, parsley flakes, 1 teaspoon salt, and black pepper.
In a 13×9×2-inch baking dish, layer half the noodles, half the ricotta filling, half the shredded mozzarella, and half the meat sauce.
Repeat the layers with the remaining noodles, ricotta filling, mozzarella, and meat sauce.
Bake at 375°F for about 30 minutes. If assembled ahead and refrigerated, bake about 45 minutes, until heated through.
Let stand for 10 minutes before slicing and serving.

title: Creamy Tomato Soup
description: A rich, silky tomato soup made with San Marzano tomatoes, sautéed onion and garlic, dried basil, heavy cream, and Parmesan. Blend smooth and season to taste.

ingredients.name: yellow onion, finely chopped or grated

steps: In a large pot over medium heat, melt the butter. Add the finely chopped or grated onion and sauté for 10 minutes.
Add the garlic and cook for another minute.
Stir in the San Marzano tomatoes, chicken broth, dried basil, sugar, salt, and pepper. Bring to a boil.
Reduce the heat and simmer for 10 minutes, partially covered.
Blend the soup until smooth using an immersion blender, or carefully blend in batches with a traditional blender, allowing steam to escape.
Return to low heat if needed. Stir in the heavy whipping cream and shredded Parmesan until the cheese melts and the soup is creamy.
Taste and adjust the salt, pepper, and sugar as desired. Serve warm.
